Orange Water

By: Jana Marx | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Dead fish. Burnt crops. Tonight on CB we look at how acid mine drainage has caused one of the biggest environmental disasters the Bronkhorstpruit area has seen in decades.

Unique Selling Point:
Biggest acid mine drainage disaster in that area in decades, but who should pay? We delve deeper into the extent of the

Summary:
Orange acid mine water from the Thungela Mine near Bronkhorstpruit has polluted the Kromdraai-spruit and the Wilge River. This has caused one of the biggest environmental issues in this area in decades.

Further information:
The majestic Wilge River on the Mpumalanga highveld is a tributary of the Olifants River. It’s the lifeblood of farmers along its banks, and benefits industries like mining. The Wilge feeds into the scenic Loskop Dam, situated in the Loskop Dam Nature Reserve. Then in February this year, tens of kilometers of water turned orange! Thousands of fish drifted to the surface… dead. Farmers couldn't irrigate with the toxic water and risked losing their whole harvest. The culprit? The Kromdraai Coal Mine, owned by a Johannesburg-based mining company, Thungela Resources. Somehow the mine had decanted its polluted wastewater into the Kromdraaispruit which empties into the Saalboomspruit... then onto the Wilge. From there, it even reached the Loskop Dam. The mine blames illegal mining for compromising the seal that ultimately resulted in the powerful discharge of mine water. But how are faceless ZamaZamas to blame for this? How large is the extent of the damage really? Will the mine's good PR (admitting that they are responsible), openness around the incident and blame-shifting to Zama-Zamas help Thungela Resources in potential legal battles?

Press Release:


Acid Alert
Dead fish, dirty water and damaged crops – it was described as one of the worst environmental disasters that the Bronkhorstspruit community had seen in years. As acid mine water polluted the Kromdraai-spruit and Wilge River, frustrated farmers pointed the finger at a nearby mine shaft, which had been sealed off for some time. So, why did a re-enforced concrete seal suddenly explode, and release thousands of litres of poisonous water into the area? Carte Blanche investigates.
Producer: Jana Marx | Presenter: Claire Mawisa


Script:


ORANGE WATER

1 VO It was the middle of February - Valentine’s Day, in fact…as Desmond Milner set out on a supply run for his farm in the Wilge River Valley…near Bronkhortspruit in Mpumalanga.

2 DESMOND ups 0:33 My pa het geboer; so 36 jaar terug het ons die plaas gekoop. Ek is die tweede generasie en my seun gaan die derde generasie Desmond wees op die plaas.

3 VO The Milner farm produces beans and soya for major food brands. Their main water source is the Wilge River - as it is for several farms in the valley. But that morning, something was very wrong…

4 Desmond UPS 01:41 Ek was die oggend vroeg… was ons gou winkel toe om diesel te gaan haal. Toe sien ons die kleur van die rivier lyk nie soos die normale kleure nie…

5 VO A healthy river usually looks brown - filled with organic matter…plants and soil. The Wilge has always snaked through the Mpumalanga Highveld - richly brown…and full of life.

6 VO Now, for kilometers, the water turned luminous.

7 Desmond VO 7:28 Vir omtrent so 3 km het hy seeblou geword en daarna het hy ‘n roesbruin geword…Ons water is gewoonlik van die skoonste riviere wat daar nog is.

8 VO As damage reports multiplied …livestock veterinarian Dr Herman de Bruin and a local helicopter pilot tracked the flow of pollution from the air.

9 Herman UPS 01;47 Hier’s geweldig baie vleilande. En ‘n vleiland se werk is om water te suiwer, maar hy kan ook net soveel doen en dan word dit oorkom, soos wat ons hier stroomop gesien het dat die vleiland naderhand vrek, dan moet jy weet jy het moeilikheid.

10 VO Around every turn in the river… They saw reeds looking burned. Thousands of fish drifted to the surface… dead.

11 Herman UPS 07:37: Geelvis was van die eerstes wat doodgegaan het.…ons het vandag soos ons gevlieg het – so ‘n karp. Dit is pragtige diere daai. Regtigwaar. So n groot karp om dood te gaan… En hoeveel het langs die rivier gedryf en hulle lê vasgespoel in die riete.

12 JACKIE UPS 9:15 Typical behaviour is that they kind of gasping at the surface and rolling over. 24;38 It's equivalent to a chemical burn on your lungs.

13 VO An aquatic scientist Dr Jackie Dabrowski was called in.

14 JACKIE UPS 12:34 I've largely coordinated the sampling effort on behalf of the Bronkhorstspruit Catchment Forum. 14:00 Once we actually got the the results back from the lab only confirmed what we actually by that stage already knew was that it was a serious acid mine drainage decant.

15 FARM LINK The spillage of mine water is a serious threat on the country’s freshwater resources. The farmers alongside the Wilge River are extremely worried about the impact the polluted water will have on their crops.

16 VO The helicopter traced the pollution back to one old coal mine. Somehow mine watewater got into the Kromdraaispruit… Saalboomspruit… and into the Wilge River down to the confluence with the Olifants River. It even reached the inflow of the Loskop Dam. Dabrowski found the spill was highly acidic at the source, with a reading of 2.5. A pH of 7 is neutral.

17 JACKIE UPS 15;26 It just goes to show how aggressive the acidity was in the water that even by the time it reached Loskop Dam, which is approximately 100 kilometers away from the source of decant, the pH was still around 4.

18 VO The source turned out to be the Kromdraai Coal Mine. With emotions running high in the community, we went to take a look. Unusually, our visit drew the attention of a large contingent of company officials and – alarmingly – armed security. Johannesburg-based Thungela Resources holds the mining rights, but Thungela stopped mining in 2020. Now, a fence and heavily armed security guards are meant to keep outsiders out.But still, large-scale Zama Zamas have infiltrated the site.

19 ONSITE MINE LINK This is where it all started – the outpouring of acid mine water that caused the worst chemical pollution in the Kromdraaispruit area in years.

20 VO Head of Corporate Affairs, Mpumi Sithole, conducted our tour on the site. (Breathe a bit) We were talking to her 2 weeks after the spill at Thungela’s office in Rosebank. We later continued our conversation at Thungela’s offices in Rosebank.

21 Mine UPS CLAIRE: 14:33 How did that water get into the rivers in the first place? 14;47 It's an underground mine working, right, which was sealed and as part of our water management strategy, it was sealed so we monitored the water quantities. 15:19 Unfortunately with the illegal mining that happens very close to the area – so illegal miners don't have the capacity to manage the water.

22 JACKIE UPS 31:20 It's groundwater that starts to fill up the chambers (ANIMATION) because you're mining below the water table, into the water table… CUT BACK TO UPSOUND: 32:15 So the situation is risky because you end up with these underground chambers that are full of water and if they develop enough head because of heavy rains or buildup of pressure over time (CUT BACK TO ANIMATION TO SHOW BURST) or the plugg or the wall or whatever is holding them back and breaks, then they will decant into the environment.

23 MINE UPS CLAIRE: 26:43 A lot of people will put the lack of security at your doorstep and say, Well, had you'd just secured it better, this would not have happened. 26:55 Look, and I understand why people will feel that way. Even in areas where we are actively mining, we still deal with the act of criminality where people just come in to steal cable.

24 VO The mine’s problem is that it has two access points - the heavily guarded entrance we used… and a national road that runs right through it.

25 MINE UPS 48:24 The National Road – as a company, we don't have jurisdiction over that…It’s a road that belongs to, that belongs to the province, so we can't fence it, we can’t block it, we don't have any jurisdiction over it.

26 VO Ten days after the spill - my flyover of the Wilge showed some colours back to normal - but farmers were still frantic about the fallout.

27 Mine UPS CLAIRE: The question on a lot of people’s minds in the area - is that it took a week… 18:22 We stopped the flow immediately when we found out. 18;27 So stopping the flow doesn't necessarily mean that there's no water that travels, right, and there's also residue or sediment that that we believe was actually activated in the water streams. We also redirected the water to ensure that it doesn't go downstream.

28 VO But for 10 days the Milners had to pause all their intensive irrigation, pending the outcome of test results to pinpoint how dangerous the chemicals in the water would be for their crops.

29 Desmond UPS 03:45 Ja, ons kon nou nie besproei nie, en veral omdat die stand so hoog is – hy is baie afhanklik van water, soos die sojas wat nou in blom is. Hy begin onder stress ingaan, dan gooi hy blommetjies – hy speen blommetjies en maak nie die volle potensiaal vrugte wat hy moet nie. 04:06 Dit affekteer jou oes dadelik.

30 VO But it’s not just the visible damage that worried Mariette Liefferink. She is the CEO of the Federation for a Sustainable Environment.

31 Mariette UPS 20;24 We can anticipate that in future there may also be an impact on, for example, fish eagles, birds, hippopotami and perhaps crocodiles that feed from these fish so so that of course has a chain reaction.

32 VO And it’s this long-term chain reaction that the farmers feel someone must pay for.

33 Desmond UPS 03:14 Dit kan jou gewas heeltemal doodmaak of dit kan jou grond affekteer. Dan gaan dit jou weer jare vat om jou grond weer te bou tot waar jy dit gehad het.

34 VO But who will pay - if the mine blames nameless, unregistered Zama Zamas?

35 MARIETTE UPS 5:52 So in terms of our National Water Act and our National Environmental Management Act…managers, operators, directors of mining companies, collectively and individually or companies must prevent pollution.

36 VO Lizette van der Walt specializes in environmental law.

37 LIZETTE UPS 2:53 The question always comes back to: Who is the current holder of the mining rights pertaining to that property? And who is the owner of that mine? 12:38 The mining rights holder remains liable ad infinitum, until the government has issued an official closure certificate.

38 ROR VO The mine has called for an investigation on how to prevent future spills.

39 MINE ROR UPS We currently brought in on board some engineers to draw up some designs to manage that, that underground, that underground mine while we still continuing, ensuring that we rehabilitate the area.

40 VO Farmers are evaluating potential damage.

41 VO And the Department of Water and Sanitation slapped Kromdraai with a Directive to stop and fix the damage…

42 VO But for the tons of dead fish… and farmers still calculating what they lost, even lawsuits and payouts will be cold comfort.

43 JACKIE UPS 20;29 This is the biggest fish kill that I have ever seen as an aquatic ecologist. And I've been working for just over a decade in this field now and I’ve investigated quite a few fish kills.

44 Desmond UPS 11;17 As hulle net kan pa-staan vir die ding en so gou as moontlik alles try regmaak…alles herstel…Vat verantwoordelikheid vir jou dade, dan is ons tevrede.

MINE OFFICE LINK Zama Zamas had been illegally mining the Thungela Kromdraai coal mine for many years now. The mine blames these highly organised, dangerous syndicates for destroying mine infrastructure and they have blame them for the recent catastrophic spillage of acid mine water in the Kromdraaispruit.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Dead fish. Burnt crops. Tonight on CB we look at how acid mine drainage has caused one of the biggest environmental disasters the Bronkhorstpruit area has seen in decades.

metadata.Summary: Orange acid mine water from the Thungela Mine near Bronkhorstpruit has polluted the Kromdraai-spruit and the Wilge River. This has caused one of the biggest environmental issues in this area in decades.
metadata.Further information: The majestic Wilge River on the Mpumalanga highveld is a tributary of the Olifants River. It’s the lifeblood of farmers along its banks, and benefits industries like mining. The Wilge feeds into the scenic Loskop Dam, situated in the Loskop Dam Nature Reserve. Then in February this year, tens of kilometers of water turned orange! Thousands of fish drifted to the surface… dead. Farmers couldn't irrigate with the toxic water and risked losing their whole harvest. The culprit? The Kromdraai Coal Mine, owned by a Johannesburg-based mining company, Thungela Resources. Somehow the mine had decanted its polluted wastewater into the Kromdraaispruit which empties into the Saalboomspruit... then onto the Wilge. From there, it even reached the Loskop Dam. The mine blames illegal mining for compromising the seal that ultimately resulted in the powerful discharge of mine water. But how are faceless ZamaZamas to blame for this? How large is the extent of the damage really? Will the mine's good PR (admitting that they are responsible), openness around the incident and blame-shifting to Zama-Zamas help Thungela Resources in potential legal battles?
